function: DQL-enhanced alternating optimization of RIS phase shifts and user power allocation, maximizing weighted sum rate and Jain fairness in a multi-user RIS network (p. 1, 5-7).
system: Passive reflecting RIS, N = 32-256 elements (3-bit phase), one AP, M = 10-50 users, Rician channels, 2.4 GHz, 20 MHz; AP antenna count not stated (p. 4, 10-11).
method: Deep Q-learning (6-dimensional state, epsilon-greedy 0.1, replay buffer 10,000, batch 32, discount 0.95) inside alternating optimization: per-element phase search and water-filling power; reinforcement learning (p. 7, 10).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician AP-user, AP-RIS, RIS-user channels (K = 5 dB), floating-intercept path loss, random 3D user positions; no 3GPP model, dataset, or measurement (p. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: DQL trained by episodes in the simulated setup; results swept over 10-50 users, N = 32-256, phase bits; no separate test scenario stated (p. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned AO and game theory; learned DRL (Fig. 2a), plus AO-only and DRL-only components (Fig. 3a); Table 4 lists transformer, meta-learning, GNN, hybrid beamforming values (p. 8, 10-12).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz), spectral efficiency, energy efficiency (bits/Hz/J), Jain's fairness index, SINR CDF, convergence iterations, latency, execution time and memory (p. 4-5, 8-12).
complexity: Execution time per component (phase 2.3 ms, power 1.8 ms, joint 3.1 ms); T(M) = 0.094M + 0.06 s, O(M) complexity; memory 12.4M + 15 MB (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "modeled using Rician fading" - custom simulator (Algorithm 1, p. 5) with floating-intercept path loss; no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "different RIS element configurations (N = 32, 64, 128, 256)" - sweeps over users and RIS size are shown, but the paper never says the trained DQL is trained at one size and tested at another or adapted; no unseen scenario, fine-tuning, or transfer is reported.
q3_support: p. 8: "DRL [35], and Game Theory [48] across varying user densities" - together with AO [47] (p. 7) these are the non-learned (AO, game theory) and learned (DRL) baselines on sum rate (Fig. 2a); the Fig. 2 legend cites other references and the DRL baseline is not described, so the reviewer should confirm.
q4_support: p. 10: "Phase Optimization (15 iterations, 2.3 ms), Power Allocation (12 iterations, 1.8 ms), and Joint Optimization (18 iterations, 3.1 ms)" - runtimes; the paper also gives T(M) = 0.094M + 0.06 s and O(M) complexity (p. 10).
q5_support: p. 10: "System parameters and simulation settings" - Table 2 defines the own simulation; no code or data link or statement is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Included: the DQL (Algorithm 5, p. 7) is the learned component acting on phase shifts and power (a_t updates Theta and p), but its action space and network are only sketched and Algorithms 2-3 are classical, so the reviewer should confirm that it performs the function. Internal inconsistencies: baselines are cited as AO [47], DRL [35], Game Theory [48] in the text (p. 7-8) but [23], [32], [29] in the Fig. 2 legend; text cites Equation (19) and Section IV-G, which do not exist; the text gives episodes up to 1000 while Fig. 3b spans about 100 epochs. q3 rests on the Fig. 2a DRL curve being an external baseline rather than the paper's own DRL-only ablation (Fig. 2e, 3a).
